[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting is based on the idea that different plants can benefit from each other's growth, health, and pest resistance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marigolds contain a chemical called alpha-terthienyl, which has been shown to be toxic to nematodes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting can improve soil health, repel pests, attract beneficial insects, provide shade and support, and enhance growth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some popular companion planting combinations include basil with tomatoes, nasturtiums with cucumbers, radishes with cucumbers, and borage with strawberries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting is not a substitute for good gardening practices like crop rotation, soil care, and integrated pest management.
